Hosting your workloads in a European data center does not automatically make your infrastructure sovereign.
True digital sovereignty requires a broader perspective.
Data sovereignty
Where is your data stored and processed? Who can access it, under which jurisdiction, and with what safeguards?
Technology sovereignty
Can your applications run across different infrastructure providers, or are they locked into proprietary platforms and services?
Operational sovereignty
Can your organization operate, maintain, recover, and evolve its infrastructure without depending entirely on a single external provider?
Infrastructure sovereignty
Who owns, manages, and controls the physical and virtual infrastructure supporting your critical applications?
AI sovereignty
Can you deploy and operate AI workloads within environments where you control the infrastructure, data flows, and access policies?
These questions are increasingly relevant as European organizations seek greater resilience and independence in their digital operations.
Digital sovereignty does not necessarily mean technological isolation. It means maintaining meaningful choices, control, and operational freedom.

What is digital sovereignty? Digital sovereignty is the ability of an organization to maintain meaningful control over its digital infrastructure, data, software, and technology decisions.
It encompasses data location, infrastructure ownership, operational independence, software dependencies, and exposure to external legal or technological risks.
Does hosting data in the EU guarantee digital sovereignty? No. EU data residency addresses an important part of digital sovereignty, but it does not automatically ensure operational independence or European control.
The ownership of the service provider, software dependencies, access to infrastructure, and applicable jurisdictions must also be considered.
How does Kubernetes support digital sovereignty? Kubernetes provides a standardized application orchestration layer that can improve portability across infrastructure environments.
Combined with open-source technologies and infrastructure automation, it can help reduce vendor lock-in and provide greater flexibility.
However, portability also depends on application architecture, storage, networking, security, and external managed services.
Can we run AI workloads on our own infrastructure? Yes. Many AI workloads can be deployed on private, on-premises, or other customer-controlled infrastructure, depending on their computational and operational requirements.
Kubernetes-based infrastructure can support workload orchestration, GPU resource management, scaling, and monitoring.
Origoss focuses on the technical infrastructure needed to deploy and operate these workloads.
Can Origoss help cloud providers build sovereign-ready services? Yes. Origoss provides Cloud Native platform engineering and integration expertise that can help cloud and IT service providers build infrastructure supporting their sovereignty objectives.
Formal compliance with EU assurance requirements also depends on legal, ownership, governance, personnel, supply-chain, and audit conditions beyond the underlying technology.
Does every organization need the highest EU sovereignty assurance level? No. The proposed EU framework is risk-based, and different public sector workloads may require different assurance levels.
Private organizations can also use the framework as a reference when evaluating their own infrastructure requirements.
Choosing the right architecture depends on the organization’s data, regulatory obligations, operational criticality, and business priorities.

From European data residency to comprehensive technological control The European Commission’s proposed Cloud and AI Development Act (CADA) introduces a common European cloud sovereignty framework built around four Union Assurance Levels.
The framework is designed primarily for cloud services used by EU institutions and public sector bodies, with assurance requirements determined according to risk and criticality.
Each level introduces progressively stronger conditions related to infrastructure location, operational independence, ownership, governance, and software supply-chain control.
For enterprises and cloud providers, these levels also offer a useful reference point when designing future-ready infrastructure strategies.
LEVEL 1 — EU Data Residency & Infrastructure Keep data and cloud infrastructure within the European Union.
Level 1 establishes the baseline for EU-based cloud services.
It requires an EU-established cloud provider, infrastructure and relevant assets located within the Union, and customer data — including metadata and telemetry — processed, stored, and transferred within the EU, subject to specified exceptions.
Additional requirements address cybersecurity, subcontractor transparency, and the governance of external support arrangements.
How Origoss Adds Value
We help organizations build Cloud Native environments that support EU data residency and infrastructure requirements.
Our technical capabilities include:
 Kubernetes platforms deployed in EU-based infrastructure. Private, hybrid, and European cloud architectures. Data residency-aware workload placement. Secure platform configuration and access control. Monitoring, logging, and infrastructure automation.  The outcome: A technically controlled, EU-hosted cloud foundation designed around your data residency and security requirements.
LEVEL 2 — Operational Independence & Supply Chain Transparency Strengthen autonomy and reduce exposure to external dependencies.
Level 2 introduces stronger requirements for operational autonomy and protection against third-country risks.
These include the location of relevant infrastructure, assets, and personnel within the EU, transparency and control over service dependencies, and safeguards addressing third-country interference.
The focus extends beyond where data resides to how services are operated, maintained, and protected.
How Origoss Adds Value
We help organizations reduce infrastructure dependencies and build more transparent, reproducible operating environments.
Our technical capabilities include:
 Vendor lock-in assessment and mitigation. Kubernetes-based portable application platforms. Infrastructure as Code and GitOps automation. Open-source infrastructure components. Software supply-chain visibility and control. Platform migration and disaster recovery architecture.  The outcome: Greater operational flexibility, improved infrastructure transparency, and reduced dependency on individual technology providers.
LEVEL 3 — European Ownership & Control Support infrastructure environments governed and controlled within Europe.
Level 3 introduces stricter requirements concerning provider ownership, control, governance, and personnel.
It places greater emphasis on who exercises effective control over a cloud service, not merely where that service operates.
The proposal also provides a mechanism under which certain third-country providers may be recognized, subject to specific conditions.
How Origoss Adds Value
We provide the engineering expertise required to build and integrate platforms that can operate within European-controlled environments.
Our technical capabilities include:
 Kubernetes platform engineering for European cloud providers. Private cloud and on-premises platform deployments. Integration with EU-based infrastructure services. Independent deployment and operations pipelines. Knowledge transfer and internal operations enablement. Cloud Native modernization of critical applications.  The outcome: An infrastructure architecture designed to support greater customer control and European operational governance.
LEVEL 4 — Comprehensive Technological Sovereignty Achieve the highest level of software supply-chain transparency and technological control.
Level 4 represents the most demanding assurance level within the proposed EU framework.
It introduces extensive requirements concerning European control, software supply-chain transparency, technological autonomy, and safeguards against third-country interference.
Meeting these requirements involves much more than selecting an EU-based cloud provider. It requires a coordinated approach covering the service provider, subcontractors, software components, operations, security, and governance.
How Origoss Adds Value
We help organizations implement technical architectures that can support demanding sovereignty objectives.
Our technical capabilities include:
 Kubernetes platforms on customer-controlled infrastructure. Open-source-based infrastructure architectures. Independently operated CI/CD and GitOps environments. Auditable deployment and configuration processes. Platform component development and integration. Automated infrastructure provisioning and lifecycle management. Long-term operational enablement and knowledge transfer.  The outcome: A highly controlled, transparent, and maintainable Cloud Native foundation designed to support advanced sovereignty requirements.
Which Sovereignty Level Does Your Organization Need? Not every workload requires the highest level of sovereignty.
The right architecture depends on data sensitivity, operational criticality, regulatory obligations, security requirements, and business priorities.
Origoss helps translate these objectives into actionable infrastructure and platform engineering decisions.
